purpose: The whole map, for the spatial view: every decision the catalogue names, built or not.
consumer: app/homelens.js wide rungs; lazily fetched, never part of the boot payload.

states.built: A dataset exists and the decision is answerable today.
states.open: Named on the map, nobody has built it yet.
states.held: Deliberately not built, with a written reason in the realm outline.
states.refused: Out of scope, with a written reason in the realm outline.

realms.label: Food and drink
realms.edge: Everything eaten or drunk, where it is bought, and where it is eaten. Food grown at home belongs here; the tools for growing it belong to Home. Food for animals belongs to Animals. Infant formula belongs to Family and care, because the decision there is about feeding a baby, not about groceries.

realms.label: Home
realms.edge: The place itself, what it runs on, what is in it, and what keeps it standing. Renting and buying belong here because where a person lives is the largest values decision most people ever make. The money instruments attached to a home, mortgages and home insurance, belong to Money. Food eaten in the home belongs to Food and drink.

families.label: Other ways to hold a home

decisions.label: Address change and utility switching services
Bulky waste, reuse and tip services
Water boilers and filters at the tap
Robot lawn mowers and outdoor smart devices

realms.label: Clothing
realms.edge: What a person wears, and every way of getting it other than buying new. Washing clothes belongs to Home, because the decision there is a detergent. Children's clothing sits in Family and care, where the sizing and the hand-me-down question live together.

realms.label: Personal care
realms.edge: What goes on a body to keep it clean, comfortable and presentable. Medicines and treatments for a condition belong to Health, and the line between them is whether a person is treating something or maintaining something. Nappies and baby toiletries belong to Family and care.

realms.label: Health
realms.edge: Treating and monitoring a body, and the services that do it. The line against Personal care is treatment against maintenance. Health insurance belongs to Money. What a gym sells is here; what a person wears to it belongs to Clothing.

decisions.label: Blood glucose monitors and diabetes supplies
Earplugs, eye masks and white noise

realms.label: Transport
realms.edge: Getting a person or a thing from one place to another, and everything owned or paid for in order to do it. Car and travel insurance belong to Money. A holiday belongs to Travel; the train that gets you there is here.

families.label: Getting a car without buying one

realms.label: Technology
realms.edge: Devices, the connections they run on, and the software and services used through them. Smart home devices belong to Home, because the decision is about the house. Streaming a film belongs to Media and culture; the television belongs here.

decisions.label: Desks, chairs and home office setup
Community forums and chat you host
Running a model on your own hardware

families.label: Knowing what is held about you

decisions.label: Data subject access and deletion tools

realms.label: Media and culture
realms.edge: What a person reads, watches, listens to, plays and makes, and the places that hold it. The device is Technology. Formal study is Learning. Libraries sit in Learning, where open knowledge is gathered.

decisions.label: Sports team ownership and supporter trusts

realms.label: Learning
realms.edge: Formal study, self-teaching, and the open knowledge anyone can reach for free. Books read for pleasure belong to Media and culture. Student loans belong to Money. Childcare belongs to Family and care, because the decision there is about care rather than about a curriculum.

decisions.label: Open licensing and public domain tools

realms.label: Travel
realms.edge: Going somewhere and staying there. The daily commute belongs to Transport; the flight and the hotel belong here. Travel insurance and travel money belong to Money, and are named here so the map does not pretend a trip is only a booking.

realms.label: Money
realms.edge: Holding money, moving it, borrowing it, growing it, and insuring against loss. Where a person banks decides what their money funds while they sleep, which is why this realm is small in spending and large in consequence. Buying a home belongs to Home; the mortgage belongs here.

decisions.label: Money management and open banking apps

realms.label: Family and care
realms.edge: Looking after people who depend on you, at both ends of a life. Children's schooling belongs to Learning. What a household buys for itself belongs to Home. Here the decision is always made on someone else's behalf, which is why it is held apart.

realms.label: Animals
realms.edge: Animals a person lives with or acts on behalf of. Meat and dairy belong to Food and drink, where the decision is about eating. Wildlife feeding in a garden belongs to Home. Here the animal is the one being provided for.

decisions.label: Pet bird and small animal food

realms.label: Work and livelihood
realms.edge: The decisions a person makes as a worker, and the small number a very small organisation makes on people's behalf. COICOP does not classify these, because they are not household consumption. They are on the map because where a person works and who represents them shapes more of a life than most purchases do, and because a catalogue that only addresses a shopper has decided in advance that a person is only a shopper.

realms.label: Civic life and giving
realms.edge: Money, time and voice given rather than spent. COICOP counts what non-profits spend on households here; this realm counts it from the other end, as the decisions a person makes about where their giving and their participation go. Buying from a mission-driven company is not giving, and belongs to Organizations.

realms.label: Organizations
realms.edge: The same catalogue read by who owns and sells a thing rather than by what the thing is. It is deliberately not a purpose category, so nothing lives here that lives elsewhere: a phone is in Technology whoever makes it. This realm answers a different question, which is who a person wants to hand money to at all.
